How to prepare for newborn photos: a step-by-step checklist

From the day you book to the day your images arrive, here’s what to do at each stage — and the things you can stop worrying about.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

To prepare for newborn photos, reserve your date in the second or third trimester, send us a message when baby arrives, and plan a full feeding, easy-off clothes and a warm, cozy car ride for session day. All you need to bring is your baby, feeding supplies, a pacifier if your baby uses one, and extra diapers — we take care of everything else.

Below is the full checklist for Rio Grande Valley families, one step at a time. It runs from pregnancy all the way to the day your edited images arrive.

In this guide

  1. Step 1: Book in your second or third trimester
  2. Step 2: Send a message when baby arrives
  3. Step 3: Pack a very short bag
  4. Step 4: Get ready the day before
  5. Step 5: The morning of your session
  6. Step 6: What happens during the 2–3 hour session
  7. Step 7: Choose your favorites at the end
  8. Questions parents ask

Step 1: Book in your second or third trimester

Preparing for newborn photos starts before baby is born. Get in touch in the second or third trimester, and a spot is saved for you around your due date. The reasons behind that timing are in our post on when to do newborn photos.

  • Choose your session. Sunshine is baby only; Wonderland adds siblings and parents.
  • Planning maternity portraits too? That’s the perfect moment to reserve the newborn session at the same time.
  • Send your request. Use the online booking form or call or text (409) 354-3075. We reply within 24 hours.
  • Reserve your date. A 50% deposit via Zelle saves your spot, and the balance is due on session day.
  • Save our number. Add it to your phone now, so it’s easy to find in the blur after delivery.

Step 2: Send a message when baby arrives

Once baby is here, send us a quick message. We’ll pick a day for your session between day 5 and day 14, Monday through Saturday by appointment. If baby comes early or late, nothing changes on your end — the date simply follows baby’s arrival.

This is an easy job to hand off. A partner, grandparent or friend can send the text while you rest, and you can join the conversation whenever you have a free hand. Keep it simple: baby is here, and you’re ready to pick a day.

If you’ve booked Wonderland, it’s also a good time to settle on family outfits. Our guide on what to wear for newborn photos has ideas for parents and siblings.

Planning your newborn session?

Adrisabel photographs families from all over the Rio Grande Valley in her private studio in the McAllen area. Send a request or call/text (409) 354-3075.

Reserve your newborn session Newborn photography

Step 3: Pack a very short bag

Here’s the complete list of what to bring. It’s short on purpose:

  • Your baby
  • Feeding supplies — whatever you’d normally pack for a few hours out
  • A pacifier, if your baby uses one
  • Extra diapers

We take care of everything else. Wraps, outfits, bonnets, headbands, little beds, baskets and backdrops are ready before you walk in, so there’s no need to buy props or pack a bag of outfits for baby. If you’re booking Wonderland, the only extra planning is what the family will wear.

Step 4: Get ready the day before

A little prep the day before keeps the morning calm. Here’s what to do:

  • Set the bag by the door. Check it against the list above, then leave it where you can’t miss it.
  • Lay out baby’s clothes. Choose something that opens at the front, like a zip-up or snap sleeper.
  • Hang up family outfits. For Wonderland, keep everyone’s clothes together so nothing gets missed in the rush.
  • Save the location. Once we’ve shared the exact session location after booking, add it to your maps app so you’re not searching for it on the day.
  • Charge your phone. You’ll want it for directions, and for a quick text to us if you’re running behind.
  • Plan your departure. Work backward from your session time, leaving room for a feeding and a few spare minutes.

Then rest as much as a newborn allows. Nothing else needs to be bought, borrowed or ironed for baby.

Step 5: The morning of your session

A calm morning helps baby arrive sleepy and settled. Three things matter most:

  • A feeding plan. Many families time a full feeding shortly before they leave, so baby starts the ride content. On a longer drive, you can also plan to feed when you arrive — there’s always time to pause. If you bottle-feed, pack one more bottle than you think you’ll need.
  • Easy-off clothes. Dress baby in that front-opening outfit, and skip anything snug, layered or fussy.
  • A warm car ride. Babies tend to stay drowsy when they’re cozy. On a cool morning, warm the car up before you buckle baby in; in a hot Valley summer, run the A/C for a few minutes first so the car is comfortable, not hot.

Have breakfast and something to drink before you go, too. The session runs about 2–3 hours, and you’ll enjoy it more if you’re not running on empty.

Driving in from farther away?

If you’re coming from the other end of the Valley, give yourself a little extra cushion. From Weslaco it’s about 20–25 minutes and from Mercedes about 25–30 minutes, while San Benito is about 40–50 minutes and Los Fresnos about 55–65 minutes. Leave 15 minutes earlier than you think you need, so a diaper change or feeding stop doesn’t make you late.

Step 6: What happens during the 2–3 hour session

The studio is warm, quiet and clean, and everything is set up before you arrive. Adrisabel photographs every session herself — she’s trained in safe newborn posing, with 15+ years of experience and hundreds of babies photographed. You can read more about Adrisabel before your day.

Your baby sets the pace. We pause for feeding, cuddles, soothing and diaper changes whenever baby needs them, which is why newborn sessions take about 2–3 hours. Every pose is gently supported, and a parent is always close by. If baby wakes, fusses or needs a feed partway through, that’s built into the plan, not a problem.

In a Wonderland session, siblings and parents join in for family portraits too. Either way, your main job is to rest, feed and cuddle when needed, and watch your baby’s first portraits take shape.

Step 7: Choose your favorites at the end

When the session wraps up, we sit together and help you choose your favorite images. There’s no proof gallery to sort through at home later — one less task during those busy newborn weeks.

Every image is hand-selected, curated and edited, and your edited images are delivered within one week. The balance is due on session day, so it’s all settled before you head home.

A little thought ahead of time makes choosing easier. Talk with your partner about where the photos will live — a nursery wall, an album, a birth announcement — and any moments you’d love to have. For anything else, our frequently asked questions page has more answers.

Getting ready for South Padre Island family photos

Soft light, breezy outfits, sandy toes and a bag packed for the kids — a practical guide to your Seaside Beach session, from planning the date to choosing your favorites.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

Great South Padre Island family photos start with a little preparation: a session timed for soft light, breezy coordinating outfits, a bag with a towel, water and a change of clothes for the kids, and an easy plan for the day. Here’s how families across the Rio Grande Valley can get ready for a Seaside Beach session with Adrisabel, step by step.

The Seaside Beach session is a family session on South Padre Island with 15 edited photos. Babies, big kids and grandparents are all welcome, and Adrisabel guides you gently the whole time — so nobody needs to know how to pose.

In this guide

  1. Timing: planned for the softest light
  2. What to wear by the water
  3. Wind and sand: small fixes that help
  4. Babies and toddlers on the beach
  5. Grandparents, cousins and twins welcome
  6. After the session: choosing your favorites
  7. Making a day of the trip
  8. Questions parents ask

Timing: planned for the softest light

The date and time of your session are planned with you for the softest light of the day. As general photography guidance, that’s usually early morning or the hour before sunset, when the sun sits low and the light turns warm and gentle.

Midday sun on the beach is bright and high overhead. It casts hard shadows under eyes, makes little ones squint and can wash out the blues of the sky and water. Softer light is kinder to skin, keeps faces relaxed and gives the sand a warm glow — and since Valley summers are hot, the gentler hours are usually more comfortable, too.

As you plan the date, think about your family’s rhythm. If your toddler is happiest in the morning, or the baby naps late in the afternoon, mention it: the time is set with you, not for you. The exact meeting spot on the island is shared when you book, so you’ll know where you’re headed well before the day.

What to wear by the water

Soft, coordinating colors look beautiful by the water. The sky, sand and sea already bring plenty of blue and warm neutrals, so gentle tones sit naturally in the scene and keep the focus on your family.

  • Colors: white, cream, sand, soft blue, blush and sage are easy choices. One brighter accent on a little one, like a red polo, can be sweet when everyone else stays soft.
  • Fabrics: breathable linen, cotton, gauze and chiffon keep everyone cooler and move nicely in a breeze. Heavy denim feels hot and holds onto sand.
  • Shapes: dresses and skirts at knee length or longer, simple button-downs, rolled linen pants and soft shorts for the kids.
  • Feet: plan on going barefoot. Sandals are fine for the walk out, but bare toes in the sand look relaxed — and nobody has to empty their shoes afterward.

Dress the grown-ups first, then the kids. When parents are in soft neutrals, little ones can wear a touch more color without anything clashing. Save the cartoon T-shirts and team jerseys for the ride home.

Planning a beach session?

Adrisabel photographs families from all over the Rio Grande Valley in her private studio in the McAllen area. Send a request or call/text (409) 354-3075.

Book your beach session Family beach sessions

Wind and sand: small fixes that help

An ocean breeze is half the charm of beach photos — it lifts hair and hems and makes everything feel alive. It can also be the trickiest part, so a few simple choices go a long way:

  • Hair: long hair looks lovely loose in a light breeze, but keep a hair tie and a few bobby pins in your pocket. A light-hold product tames flyaways without looking stiff.
  • Hats and sunglasses: wide hats tend to blow away and sunglasses hide eyes, so keep both in the bag during photos.
  • Skirts: a lining or a little weight in the fabric keeps a breezy dress pretty rather than unruly. Very short, very sheer pieces are hard to manage in the wind.
  • Sand: leave sentimental jewelry at home, zip phones and keys into a bag, and brush off little hands before they rub their eyes.
  • Sunscreen: apply it well before the session so it has time to sink in, and choose a non-greasy formula for faces.

Most of all, don’t fight it. A little wind in your hair and sand on your knees are part of what makes beach photos feel real.

Babies and toddlers on the beach

Babies and toddlers are more than welcome, and there’s no need to keep them perfectly still or perfectly clean. A little planning on your side helps them stay happy:

  • Pack the bag: bring a towel, water and a change of clothes for the kids. Wet hems and sandy bottoms happen fast.
  • Arrive fed and rested: a snack and a nap beforehand make a big difference, so plan the drive around nap time if you can.
  • Let them explore: toddlers rarely stand still by the ocean, and they don’t need to. Digging, chasing the edge of the water and collecting shells make wonderful, natural pictures.
  • Babies who aren’t walking yet: a towel or blanket on the sand gives them a soft, clean spot to sit.
  • Save the big splash for last: once clothes are soaked, they stay that way, so let the kids run into the waves at the end.

Grandparents, cousins and twins welcome

Grandparents and extended family are welcome, and few things are sweeter than three generations together on the sand. A little coordination beforehand keeps it easy:

  • Make a short list of the groupings you’d love — everyone together, grandparents with the grandkids, each household on its own, just the cousins.
  • Share your color palette with every household so outfits work together.
  • Soft sand can be tiring to walk on, so make sure older relatives have easy shoes for the walk out and a chance to rest between groupings.

Your session includes 15 edited photos, so it helps to decide which groupings matter most. Expecting twins, or already chasing two toddlers the same age? Twins can be added to any package and include 4 extra photos — just let us know when you book.

After the session: choosing your favorites

After the session, we sit together and help you choose your favorite images, so there’s no proof gallery to sort through at home. Every image is hand-selected, curated and edited, and your photos are delivered within one week.

A few questions make choosing easier:

  • Which one would you frame for the wall? Often it’s a wide shot of everyone with the water behind you.
  • Which close-ups capture each child right now — sandy toes, a big laugh, a quiet cuddle?
  • Is there a moment that simply feels like your family, even if nobody is looking at the camera?

If you can’t narrow it down to 15, extra edited photos can be added to any session.

Making a day of the trip

If you’re driving in from McAllen, Edinburg, Brownsville or anywhere else in the Rio Grande Valley, your session is a lovely excuse to make a day of it. A few choices keep it relaxed:

  • Leave generous time for the drive and for finding the meeting spot, so nobody arrives rushed.
  • For an evening session, plan a slow day — an easy lunch, a nap for the little ones, then outfits on shortly before you head out.
  • For an early session, the rest of the day is yours: breakfast, a walk along the beach, a swim once the photos are done.
  • Pack a bag for wet, sandy clothes and keep a towel on the car seat for the ride home.

A beach session also pairs nicely with other chapters — a newborn session, baby milestone portraits through the first year, or a first-birthday cake smash (our first birthday photoshoot ideas might spark a plan). When you’re ready, reserve your Seaside Beach session and we’ll plan the date and time together.

What to wear for maternity photos (and what to leave at home)

From studio gowns to comfortable shoes, here’s how to choose outfits that show your bump, suit a soft studio look and bring the whole family together.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

The short answer to what to wear for maternity photos: something that shows the shape of your bump — fitted or softly flowing — in a solid, gentle color and a fabric that drapes. Studio gowns are available too, so you can wear one of those or bring your own favorites.

Since every maternity session happens indoors, in Adrisabel’s private studio in the McAllen area, you can dress for comfort and the camera instead of Rio Grande Valley weather. Below, we’ll go through shapes, colors and fabrics, how to dress your partner and kids, and the small details that make the day easier.

In this guide

  1. Start with the studio gowns
  2. Pick shapes that show your bump
  3. Soft, solid colors for a soft studio look
  4. Fabrics that drape — and what to leave at home
  5. Coordinate your partner and kids without matching
  6. Shoes, hair, makeup and a couple of backups
  7. Next up: your newborn session
  8. Questions parents ask

Start with the studio gowns

Studio gowns are available for maternity sessions, and they’re often the easiest place to start. Choosing one takes a shopping trip off your list and gives you an elegant look without buying something you may wear only once.

When you reach out, ask about the gowns and mention anything you’re thinking of bringing yourself. Adrisabel helps you plan outfits and colors that feel like you, so whatever you choose works with your partner and kids. You can read more about the session on our maternity photography page.

Still deciding on a date? Our guide on when to take maternity photos covers timing. This one is all about getting dressed.

Pick shapes that show your bump

Your bump is the heart of these portraits, so choose pieces that let its shape show. Two approaches work especially well:

  • Fitted: a stretchy knit or ribbed dress, or a fitted top, that follows the curve of your belly. It’s clean and modern, and the shape reads clearly from every angle.
  • Flowing: a long, soft dress that skims over the bump and falls loosely below it. A wrap style, or a waistline that sits above the bump, keeps the fabric from hiding your shape.

What tends to work less well: boxy tunics, oversized sweaters and stiff layers that cover the bump completely. If you love a cozy cardigan, wear it open over a fitted dress so the curve still shows.

Before the day, sit down in each outfit, lift your arms and walk around the room. If something pulls, pinches or rides up at home, it will bother you during the session too.

Expecting?

Adrisabel photographs families from all over the Rio Grande Valley in her private studio in the McAllen area. Send a request or call/text (409) 354-3075.

Ask about maternity Maternity photography

Soft, solid colors for a soft studio look

Solid colors keep the attention on you, your bump and the people you love. Gentle tones suit a soft studio look especially well, and they tend to feel timeless when you look back years from now.

  • White, ivory and cream
  • Blush, dusty rose and mauve
  • Sage, soft blue and muted teal
  • Oatmeal, taupe and warm beige

A deeper shade, such as burgundy, olive or navy, can look beautiful on a partner, as long as the overall palette stays calm. If you can’t decide between two colors you love, bring both and talk them through with Adrisabel.

Fabrics that drape — and what to leave at home

Fabric makes more of a difference than most people expect. Pieces that drape, such as jersey, chiffon, soft knits, lace and tulle, fall naturally around the bump and move gently when you turn. Stiff fabrics tend to crease, stand away from the body and blur your shape.

A few things are best left in the closet:

  • Logos and slogans: words pull the eye away from faces.
  • Busy prints: loud patterns, tiny checks and thin stripes can look distracting on camera.
  • Neon and very bright colors: they can reflect color onto skin.
  • Anything untested: try new pieces on, and wash them if needed, well before the day.

Hang or steam everything the night before. Wrinkles are easy to miss at home and hard to miss in a portrait.

Coordinate your partner and kids without matching

Partners and big brothers and sisters are welcome, and dressing everyone is easier than it sounds. Aim for a shared palette rather than identical outfits: pick two or three colors from your own look and let everyone else wear a variation of them.

  • Partner: a solid button-down, a soft knit polo or a fine sweater in a neutral or a deeper shade from your palette. Simple and well fitting beats trendy.
  • Kids: soft solids with a little texture — knit, linen, a cotton dress — and nothing stiff or scratchy that will make them restless.
  • Everyone: a similar level of dressiness. If you’re in a long gown, jeans and a T-shirt beside you will stand out.

A few days before the session, lay all the outfits out together on a bed and take a quick photo with your phone. Anything that jumps out on the screen will jump out in the portraits, too.

Shoes, hair, makeup and a couple of backups

Shoes: wear something comfortable for getting there — flats, sandals or clean sneakers. Feet often swell later in pregnancy, and with a long dress your shoes usually won’t show anyway.

Hair and makeup: as a general tip, choose a polished version of your everyday look rather than something brand new. Matte or satin-finish makeup tends to photograph better than very shiny products. If you’re booking a stylist, a trial run takes away the guesswork.

Hands and jewelry: hands often rest on or around the bump in maternity portraits, so tidy nails in a neutral shade are worth a few minutes. Keep jewelry simple — your rings and one delicate piece are plenty.

Options: bring two or three outfits, steamed and on hangers, with the shoes and accessories for each. If you’re driving in from elsewhere in the Valley — Harlingen is about 40–45 minutes away, Brownsville about 60–70 minutes — hang them in the car rather than folding them into a bag.

Next up: your newborn session

Once your maternity outfits are sorted, the next chapter is closer than it feels. If you haven’t already, reserve your newborn session when you book maternity — we’ll save a spot around your due date and set the session within those first 5–14 days.

The good news is that newborn day takes far less wardrobe planning. Baby milestone photos through the first year, month by month

Babies change every few weeks. Here’s what each stage tends to look like, what a sitter session is, and how to choose between one session and a whole-year plan.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

The best time for baby milestone photos is whenever your baby is learning something new: first smiles around 1–2 months, giggles at 3–4, sitting with a little help at 5–6, sitting solo at 7–8, and crawling and pulling up at 9–10 months. You can capture one of those chapters with a single session, or follow every one of them with a first-year plan.

Below is a month-by-month look at the first year, what the 6 month baby photoshoot and the sitter session are all about, and how Rio Grande Valley families plan a year of photos without the pressure. It all ends, of course, with cake.

In this guide

  1. The first year, month by month
  2. Why the 6 month baby photoshoot is a favorite
  3. What is a sitter session?
  4. One chapter or the whole year: Fairytale or Pixie Dust?
  5. Real smiles, without the pressure
  6. Finish the year with a Cake Smash
  7. Questions parents ask

The first year, month by month

Every baby keeps their own timeline, so think of these as loose chapters rather than deadlines. Here’s what each stage often looks like, and what tends to photograph beautifully:

  • 1–2 months: sleepy snuggles, tiny hands and the very first smiles. Close-ups and in-arms portraits with mom or dad shine at this age.
  • 3–4 months: head up, giggles and big, curious eyes. Tummy-time portraits catch that proud, wobbly head lift and those first real laughs.
  • 5–6 months: rolling, reaching and sitting with a little help. Babies grab at everything now, so a favorite toy becomes a natural prop.
  • 7–8 months: sitting up on their own, with lots of personality. Free hands mean clapping, waving and plenty of expressions.
  • 9–10 months: crawling, pulling up and busy, happy exploring. Photos fill with motion — a crawl toward the camera, a peek over the edge of a basket.
  • 12 months: the first birthday, and usually a cake. More on that at the end.

Not sure which stage to photograph? Think about the moment you’d most hate to forget. For many parents it’s the first real smile; for others, it’s the day their baby sat up and looked so proud of it.

Why the 6 month baby photoshoot is a favorite

Six months sits right in the middle of the first year, and it’s one of the most rewarding ages to photograph. Your baby is alert and expressive, reaches for everything, and is starting to sit with a little help — so you get real interaction without a baby who crawls out of the frame.

It’s also the age when many babies discover their own feet and find everything fascinating. A few ideas worth planning for:

  • Sitting propped in a soft basket, with a parent’s hands close by.
  • Tummy-time portraits, head up and eyes right on you.
  • Reaching for a favorite toy, focused little frown and all.
  • Toes in hand — a classic six-month pose that babies strike all on their own.

If you’d like just one session, Fairytale fits a 6-month shoot perfectly. On the Pixie Dust plan, Option B includes a session right at 6 months, while Option A catches the stages on either side at 5 and 7 months.

Planning baby’s first year?

Adrisabel photographs families from all over the Rio Grande Valley in her private studio in the McAllen area. Send a request or call/text (409) 354-3075.

Plan your milestone sessions Baby & milestone photography

What is a sitter session?

“Sitter session” is a term photographers use for a session timed to when a baby can sit up steadily on their own. For many babies that happens somewhere around 6 to 8 months, though every baby gets there in their own time.

It’s a sweet in-between stage. Your baby can sit, look around and engage with you, but usually isn’t crawling off in every direction yet. With hands free for clapping and reaching, their personality shows up in nearly every frame.

A good rule of thumb is to reach out when your baby is starting to sit with a little help, so the session lands as they find their balance. A Fairytale session works beautifully as a sitter session, and both Pixie Dust schedules include a visit in this window — 7 months in Option A, and 6 and 8 months in Option B.

One chapter or the whole year: Fairytale or Pixie Dust?

There are two ways to photograph your baby’s first year with us. The right one depends on how much of the story you want to tell.

Fairytale: one favorite chapter

Fairytale is a single session for babies from 2 to 11 months. It includes 8 edited photos, two outfits and two backdrops. It’s a lovely choice if there’s one stage you don’t want to miss — first smiles, giggles or sitting up — and you can book a Fairytale session whenever that stage arrives.

Pixie Dust: five sessions, one whole year

The Pixie Dust plan follows your baby through five sessions during the first year. You choose one of two schedules:

  • Option A: 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 months
  • Option B: 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 months

Each session includes 8 edited images, with a new outfit and a new backdrop every time, so the collection grows into a complete first-year story. Siblings and parents are included, too, so big brother, big sister, mom and dad can join in.

Choosing a schedule? Option A begins soon after newborn photos and ends with a crawler at 9 months. Option B lands right on the 6-month mark and finishes at 10 months, closer to the first birthday. You can reserve the Pixie Dust plan or learn more on our baby milestone photography page.

Real smiles, without the pressure

Babies don’t smile on command, and they shouldn’t have to. Our baby sessions are built around your little one’s mood, with play breaks, snacks and silly songs whenever they’re needed — a fussy few minutes is a pause, not a problem.

  • Come fed and rested. Choose a time near your baby’s happiest part of the day, and bring a bottle or snack for quick resets.
  • Bring the favorites. A beloved toy or the song that always works can coax out a grin in seconds.
  • Skip the “say cheese.” Peekaboo, a funny noise or a parent’s face just behind the camera works far better than asking for a smile.
  • Stay relaxed. Babies pick up on the mood in the room, and a calm parent helps make a calm baby.

Adrisabel photographs every session herself, so on the Pixie Dust plan your baby sees the same familiar face at each visit. With 15+ years of experience and hundreds of babies photographed, she knows the best smile is usually the one you wait for.

We welcome families from all over the RGV, and with five sessions in a year, the drive is worth planning. From Edinburg it’s about 15–20 minutes, from San Benito about 40–50 minutes and from Los Fresnos about 55–65 minutes.

Finish the year with a Cake Smash

After a year of milestones, the first birthday deserves its own celebration. The Pixie Dust plan doesn’t include the 1-year Cake Smash — it’s booked separately — so many families reserve it as their last milestone session approaches.

That session comes with its own timeless cake and backdrop, plus 8 edited photos — an easy, joyful bookend to the year. For inspiration, browse our first birthday photoshoot ideas, or start with what a smash cake is if it’s all new to you.

After each session along the way, you’ll choose your favorites with us before heading home, and the edited images arrive within one week. By the time your baby turns one, you’ll have a whole year of chapters to look back on — and no unsorted gallery waiting at home.

Cake smashNovember 11, 20265 min read

First birthday photoshoot ideas that feel like your baby

A classic cake smash, quiet portraits and a few frames with the people they love — plus outfit tips and how to plan the session around naps and snacks.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

The best first birthday photoshoot ideas are simple: a classic cake smash, a few clean portraits, and photos with the people your baby loves most. Add a comfortable outfit and a session time that fits your baby’s naps, and the rest tends to fall into place.

Below are the ideas we share most often with families across the Rio Grande Valley. We’ll cover what works, what to skip, and how to spread photos through the first year so the birthday is the happy ending rather than the only chapter.

In this guide

  1. Idea 1: A classic cake smash
  2. Idea 2: Clean, timeless portraits
  3. Idea 3: Bring in siblings and parents
  4. Idea 4: An outfit your baby can actually move in
  5. Idea 5: Plan the day around naps and snacks
  6. Idea 6: Make the birthday the last chapter, not the only one
  7. Questions parents ask

Idea 1: A classic cake smash

There’s a reason the cake smash tops so many first birthday lists: one-year-olds and frosting are a natural match. The classic look is beautifully simple, and in many of our cake smash photos you’ll see the same clean pieces — a white cake, big white ONE letters and white balloons against a single soft backdrop.

With Adrisabel, the cake comes with the session, along with a timeless backdrop and eight edited photos, so there’s nothing for you to order or carry in. If you’re curious about the cake itself, our smash cake size and frosting guide covers the details.

One tip worth knowing: some of the sweetest frames happen before the first touch. The curious stare, the hand to the mouth, the slow reach toward the frosting — give your baby a quiet moment with the cake before anyone cheers them on.

Idea 2: Clean, timeless portraits

Not every first birthday photo needs a prop. Some of the most lasting images are the simplest ones: your baby against a plain backdrop, in soft light, doing what one-year-olds do — clapping, babbling, inspecting their own toes. A few portrait ideas to keep in mind:

  • Hands and feet. Those dimpled knuckles and chubby toes change fast.
  • An almost-walking moment. If your baby is pulling up, holding a parent’s fingers makes a sweet, steady portrait.
  • The look-back. A glance over the shoulder toward mom or dad is natural and completely unposed.
  • The in-between face. A quiet pause between giggles often shows the most of who your baby is.

Simple portraits age well because nothing in them dates the picture. Years from now, the details of the set will matter far less than the look on your baby’s face.

Planning the big ONE?

Adrisabel photographs families from all over the Rio Grande Valley in her private studio in the McAllen area. Send a request or call/text (409) 354-3075.

Reserve your cake smash Cake smash photography

Idea 3: Bring in siblings and parents

Your baby’s first year was a team effort. A photo of big sister holding the baby’s hand, or of mom and dad lifting the birthday baby between them, shows who was there for every part of it. Ideas that tend to work well with one-year-olds:

  • A big sibling leaning in for a cheek kiss — or a high five, if kisses are officially “gross.”
  • Baby on a parent’s lap, the two of them looking at each other instead of the camera.
  • Parents’ hands wrapped around baby’s hands — a lovely echo if you have similar newborn photos.
  • A cuddle with grandparents at the party itself. Ask a friend to catch it on your phone so no one has to pose.

The Cake Smash session keeps the spotlight on your birthday baby. If family photos are high on your list, the Pixie Dust plan includes siblings and parents, so the whole crew can be part of the months leading up to the cake. Hoping for a family frame on cake day, too? Just ask when you book.

Idea 4: An outfit your baby can actually move in

The best outfit for a first birthday photoshoot is one your baby forgets they’re wearing. A comfortable one-year-old will crawl, reach, sit and grin; one who’s tugging at a scratchy collar won’t.

  • Comfort first. Choose soft, stretchy fabrics with no itchy tags, stiff waistbands or tight elastic.
  • Simple over busy. Solid colors and gentle patterns photograph better than big logos, characters or slogans.
  • Coordinate with the backdrop. In our photos, a blue fish-print outfit looks lovely on aqua, and a floral tulle dress with a pearl flower crown glows against pink.
  • Accessories only if your baby agrees. A headband or flower crown is darling for as long as it stays on — and if it keeps coming off, let it go.
  • Bare feet are fine. Little shoes tend to come off anyway, and tiny toes are part of the charm.
  • Do a fit check a few days early. Babies grow quickly, and a short try-on saves surprises on session day.

For the cake portion, think washable. Frosting finds its way into every fold, which is why we suggest packing a spare outfit for the drive home.

Idea 5: Plan the day around naps and snacks

The most important planning choice isn’t the theme — it’s the time of day. A rested, fed one-year-old is curious and game, while a baby who skipped a nap won’t be, no matter how lovely the setup.

  • Book a few weeks ahead. Reaching out early gives you the best chance at a time that fits your baby’s nap schedule instead of squeezing around it. We take appointments Monday through Saturday and reply within 24 hours.
  • Aim for just after a nap. For some babies that’s mid-morning, for others it’s after lunch — you know your baby’s best window.
  • Pack a favorite snack. A familiar treat can turn a fussy moment around, and snack breaks are a normal part of our baby sessions.
  • Keep the shoot apart from the party. A party day is loud and exciting, and a quieter day usually means a calmer baby.
  • Count the drive. From Weslaco it’s about 20–25 minutes, from Harlingen about 40–45 minutes and from Rio Grande City about 45–50 minutes. A short car nap on the way can work in your favor.

Idea 6: Make the birthday the last chapter, not the only one

First birthday photos mean even more when you can set them beside photos from the months before. Many RGV families plan the year in pieces:

  • Newborn photos in the sleepy first 5–14 days — see the best time for newborn photos for the details.
  • A Fairytale session for one favorite chapter between 2 and 11 months — first smiles, giggles or sitting up.
  • Or the Pixie Dust plan — five sessions on the odd months from 1 to 9 (Option A) or the even months from 2 to 10 (Option B). Our baby milestone photography page has the details.
  • Then the Cake Smash at one year, to finish the story.

One thing to know as you plan: the Pixie Dust plan does not include the Cake Smash. It’s booked separately, so plan to reserve your cake date a few weeks before the birthday. When you’re ready, you can request a Cake Smash date or compare all sessions & packages.

What to wear for newborn photos: easy outfits for the whole family

Baby’s wardrobe is already waiting at the studio. Here’s how parents and big brothers and sisters can dress so your family portraits feel soft, timeless and true to you.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

For newborn photos, your baby doesn’t need anything special to wear — wraps, outfits, bonnets and headbands are all provided by the studio, so just dress baby in something easy to take off. If you’re joining the photos, choose soft, timeless colors and comfortable, fitted clothes that coordinate with each other rather than match.

Here’s what that looks like for each person in the frame. These tips are written for Rio Grande Valley families planning a Wonderland newborn and family session, from mom and dad to the littlest big sibling.

In this guide

  1. What baby wears: it’s all provided
  2. What to wear for newborn family photos: soft, timeless colors
  3. Coordinate, don’t match
  4. Choose comfortable, fitted clothes
  5. A comfortable postpartum outfit for mom
  6. Dressing little siblings for comfort
  7. Bring something meaningful from home
  8. Questions parents ask

What baby wears: it’s all provided

The studio is stocked with wraps, outfits, bonnets and headbands, plus little beds, baskets and backdrops, all in soft, timeless colors. That means there’s no need to shop for a special newborn outfit or guess at sizes before baby arrives.

On session day, dress baby in whatever is easiest to take off. A zip-up or snap-front sleeper works well because it comes off without pulling anything over baby’s head. Skip tight elastic, which can leave little lines on delicate skin, and outfits with lots of tiny buttons.

Still working out your dates? Our guide on when to do newborn photos explains the sleepy 5–14 day window and how your session day is set.

What to wear for newborn family photos: soft, timeless colors

The backdrops and setups at the studio come in soft, timeless colors, so family outfits look most natural in a similar gentle palette. Think cream, ivory, white, oatmeal, khaki, taupe or soft gray, with a quiet accent like dusty rose, sage or pale blue if you’d like a touch of color.

These tones keep the focus on faces and on baby, and they won’t look dated when you look back at the photos years from now. Browsing the portfolio is an easy way to see which shades feel most like your family.

What to leave in the closet: neon and very bright colors, big logos, cartoon characters and slogans, and busy prints like bold stripes or large plaids. They pull the eye away from baby and can reflect color onto faces. If you love pattern, keep it small and subtle, and give it to just one person.

Dark colors like black or navy can work in small doses. Head-to-toe dark clothing, though, tends to feel heavy next to a newborn wrapped in cream and soft knits.

Planning your newborn session?

Reserve your newborn session Newborn photography

Coordinate, don’t match

Identical white tops and jeans can look a little stiff. Instead, aim for outfits that coordinate: similar tones and a similar level of dressiness, spread across a few shades. Mom in a cream knit, dad in a khaki button-down and a big brother in a soft gray sweater look like they belong together without looking like a uniform.

Texture is what keeps a soft palette from looking flat. Chunky knits, linen, soft cotton, gentle lace and ribbing all look lovely next to a baby wrapped in knit, while very shiny or stiff fabrics tend to feel less cozy on camera.

An easy way to plan is to start with one outfit, often mom’s, and build everyone else’s around its colors. A few days before your session, lay everyone’s outfits side by side on the bed. If one piece jumps out, swap it for something quieter, then steam or hang everything, since creases show more on light fabrics.

Choose comfortable, fitted clothes

Family portraits usually mean sitting close together, leaning in and holding baby, so comfort matters as much as color. Clothes that fit well — not tight, not baggy — keep clean lines in photos and let you move easily. For dads and partners, a soft polo, henley or light sweater in a neutral tone is an easy choice.

The studio is kept warm for baby, so breathable fabrics will keep you comfortable. And since Valley summers run hot, a light knit or linen will feel better than a heavy sweater on the drive over.

Keep accessories simple. Delicate jewelry and wedding rings look lovely in close-ups with baby’s tiny hands and feet, while chunky bracelets, long necklaces and big watches can get in the way when you’re holding a newborn.

A comfortable postpartum outfit for mom

In the newborn window, you’re only a week or two past giving birth, so choose something that feels good on your body today. Soft, stretchy fabrics and forgiving shapes — a flowy dress, a wrap dress or a knit top with soft pants — are easier to sit, lean and hold baby in than anything structured.

Skip tight waistbands and anything you’d need to tug at between poses. A light layer, like a long cardigan over a simple dress, is easy to adjust if you get warm and adds soft texture to the photos. Keep hair and makeup close to your everyday look, too.

Most of all, wear something that feels like you. When you’re comfortable, it shows in your face and in the way you hold your baby.

Dressing little siblings for comfort

Big brothers and sisters are happiest in clothes they can sit, play and wiggle in. Soft knits, cotton dresses, overalls and simple sweaters in the family palette look sweet next to a newborn and won’t scratch. Skip itchy tags, stiff collars and anything they’ll want to pull off after ten minutes. For the littlest big siblings who are still crawling, soft leggings or a romper make sitting and scooting easy.

Let older kids choose between two outfits you’ve already picked. Having a say helps them feel part of the day, and a comfortable child is far easier to photograph than an unhappy one in a “perfect” outfit.

Dress toddlers last, right before you leave, so outfits stay clean on the way. A spare top in the car is a good backup for little ones who love a snack.

Bring something meaningful from home

You’re welcome to bring a meaningful item from home. It might be a blanket a grandparent made, a tiny outfit an older sibling once wore, a family heirloom or a small stuffed animal from the nursery. One or two special pieces are plenty. If a piece is fragile or one of a kind, mention it when you arrive.

Questions parents ask

Do parents need to dress up for a baby-only Sunshine session?

No. Sunshine is a baby-only session, so wear whatever is comfortable and dress your little one in something easy to take off. The outfit planning in this guide is for Wonderland, where siblings and parents join the photos.

What should I wear if I’m breastfeeding during the session?

Choose a top or dress that opens at the front or wraps, so you can feed during the pauses without changing. A soft cardigan over a nursing tank works well too.

Can I wear something from my maternity wardrobe?

Yes. Soft, stretchy maternity dresses and tops are often the most comfortable choice in the first weeks after birth — just pick one in a color that fits your family’s palette.

NewbornOctober 14, 20265 min read

When to do newborn photos: the sleepy first two weeks

The short answer is 5 to 14 days after birth. Here’s why that window works so well, when to reserve your spot, and what to do if your baby is already a little older.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

The best time to do newborn photos is between 5 and 14 days after birth, when most babies sleep deeply and still curl up the way they did before they were born. To be sure of a spot in that window, book during your second or third trimester — the exact date is set once your baby arrives.

Below, we walk through when to do newborn photos for families across the Rio Grande Valley. You’ll find why those first two weeks work so well, how booking and scheduling happen, what changes if baby comes early or late, and your options if your little one is already a bit older.

In this guide

  1. Why days 5–14 are the sweet spot
  2. When to book: your second or third trimester
  3. How the date is set when baby arrives
  4. Choosing the best day within the window
  5. Already past the newborn window? Here are your options
  6. Planning the drive from across the Valley
  7. Questions parents ask

Why days 5–14 are the sweet spot

In the first two weeks, most newborns spend long stretches in a deep, heavy sleep. They’re also still used to being snug and tucked in, so they settle easily into the soft, curled-up poses people picture when they think of newborn portraits — knees tucked, tiny hands near the face, wrapped in a soft knit.

That sleepiness is what keeps the session calm. Moving from a wrap on a little bed to a basket takes only small, gentle adjustments, and a sleepy baby usually stays settled through them. Adrisabel is trained in safe newborn posing and has photographed hundreds of babies, so each change is made slowly and with care.

Starting around day 5 leaves the first few days for rest, recovery and getting home. After about two weeks, many babies are awake for longer and like to stretch out, and they’re often less content in tightly curled poses. That’s a normal, lovely change — it simply means a different kind of session suits them better.

When to book: your second or third trimester

So when should you do newborn photos if baby isn’t here yet? Reach out during your second or third trimester, and we’ll save a spot around your due date. Booking early takes one more decision off your plate before those tired first days at home.

This is also when you choose your session. Sunshine is all about baby, with 8 edited photos, 2 outfits and 2 backdrops. Wonderland brings in siblings and parents, with 15 edited photos, 2 outfits and 4 backdrops. You can compare both on our newborn photography page.

If you’re planning maternity portraits too, booking maternity is the perfect time to reserve your newborn session as well. Our guide on when to take maternity photos covers the bump side of the timeline.

Planning your newborn session?

Adrisabel photographs families from all over the Rio Grande Valley in her private studio in the McAllen area. Send a request or call/text (409) 354-3075.

Reserve your newborn session Newborn photography

How the date is set when baby arrives

When your little one is born, just send us a message — a call or text to (409) 354-3075 works, or a note through the booking form. We reply within 24 hours and set your session for a day within the 5–14 day window. There’s no need to do the math yourself; just tell us the birth date, and we’ll count the days.

Early or late babies are completely normal. Your due date is a guide, not a deadline, so the session is set when baby actually arrives. Whether your little one comes two weeks early or a week late, the plan stays the same: send a message, and we’ll find a day inside the window.

Expecting twins?

Twins can be added to any package and include 4 extra photos. They often arrive a little ahead of schedule, and that’s fine too — let us know when they’re here, and their session is set within the same 5–14 day window.

Choosing the best day within the window

There’s no single right day between day 5 and day 14, so deciding when to take newborn photos within that window comes down to your family’s week. Some parents like to come in closer to day 5, while everything still feels brand new; others prefer a few more days at home to rest and settle into feeding first.

Both work well. A few quick questions can help you choose:

  • Is your partner free on certain days? Sessions run Monday through Saturday by appointment (we’re closed Sundays), so a Saturday may be easier if work is a factor.
  • Are big brothers or sisters joining? For a Wonderland session, pick a time of day when they’re usually rested and happy.
  • What else is on the calendar? Those first two weeks often include checkups for baby and for mom, so choose a day with nothing else scheduled.
  • How are you feeling? Recovery looks different for everyone, so take the extra days if you need them.

Already past the newborn window? Here are your options

Maybe the first weeks flew by, or you’re only now starting to think about photos. That’s okay. The 5–14 day window is ideal for sleepy, curled-up portraits, but it isn’t the only time to photograph your baby.

  • Almost two weeks old: send a Sunshine newborn session request right away, so we can look for a day before the window closes.
  • A few weeks old: Wonderland is for newborns and babies with the whole family, so it’s a lovely choice when you want baby, siblings and parents together in the photos. To follow the whole first year instead, Pixie Dust includes 5 milestone sessions, starting at 1 or 2 months.
  • Two months and up: Fairytale is our baby session for 2–11 months, made for first smiles, giggles and sitting up.

The photos change in a good way, too. Instead of tightly curled, sleepy poses, you get wide-open eyes, little expressions and, before long, those first smiles.

Babies don’t smile on command, so sessions for older little ones are built around baby’s mood, with play breaks, snacks and silly songs. You can read about each stage on our baby milestone photography page.

Planning the drive from across the Valley

Families come to the studio in the McAllen area from all over the RGV, so it’s worth thinking about the drive when you pick your day. From McAllen and Pharr, it’s just minutes. Mission is about 10–20 minutes away and Edinburg about 15–20 minutes, while Harlingen is about 40–45 minutes, Rio Grande City about 45–50 minutes and Brownsville about 60–70 minutes.

A newborn session takes about 2–3 hours, so with a longer drive on each end, it can fill a good part of the day. Keep the rest of that day light, and if a partner or grandparent can drive, mom can rest on the way there and back. The exact session location is shared after booking.

Cake smashOctober 14, 20265 min read

What is a smash cake? A simple guide to the big ONE

It’s a little cake made for one very important guest. Here’s what size to choose, what to put on top and how a cake smash session works in our McAllen-area studio.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

A smash cake is a small cake made just for the birthday baby to dig into — usually at the first birthday. A common size is a single round cake about 4 to 6 inches across: small enough for little hands, and big enough to look like a real celebration in photos.

Guests share the party cake, but the smash cake belongs to one tiny person — no forks, no plates, no rules. Below, we walk through size, frosting and flavor, and how a cake smash session works with Adrisabel for families across the Rio Grande Valley.

In this guide

  1. Smash cake or cake smash — what’s the difference?
  2. What size is a smash cake?
  3. Frosting and flavor: keep it soft and simple
  4. How a cake smash session works with Adrisabel
  5. Dive in or careful poke — both make wonderful pictures
  6. When to book your cake smash
  7. Questions parents ask

Smash cake or cake smash — what’s the difference?

You’ll hear both phrases, and they’re close cousins. The smash cake is the cake itself — a mini cake set in front of your one-year-old to touch, squish, taste and explore however they like. A cake smash is the moment, or the photo session, built around it.

At a party, the smash cake usually sits beside a larger cake that gets sliced and shared. At a photo session, it becomes the center of a simple setup, styled so the attention stays on your baby’s hands, face and very first reaction.

Why do parents love it? A first birthday is a milestone for the whole family, but the smash cake gives your little one a celebration that’s entirely their own. It also brings out expressions you won’t see on any other day.

What size is a smash cake?

Smash cakes are usually small and simple — one short round cake rather than a tiered showpiece. Most fall somewhere between 4 and 6 inches across, often two or three short layers tall. That’s plenty for a one-year-old, who isn’t meant to finish it, only to explore it.

  • Around 4 inches: a petite, sweet option, especially if the cake is mainly for a quick moment at the party.
  • Around 6 inches: a nice fit for photos, with enough frosting to dig into and enough height to read as a real cake on camera.
  • Taller or tiered: better saved for the guest cake. A tall, narrow cake can tip over once small hands get involved.

How big is a smash cake compared with the party cake?

Much smaller. A party cake is sized to serve your guests, while a smash cake is sized for one pair of hands. If you’re ordering both, it’s common to ask for the smash cake as a mini version of the party cake, so the two look like a matching set.

Planning the big ONE?

Adrisabel photographs families from all over the Rio Grande Valley in her private studio in the McAllen area. Send a request or call/text (409) 354-3075.

Reserve your cake smash Cake smash photography

Frosting and flavor: keep it soft and simple

Because the cake is for touching as much as tasting, soft frosting like buttercream or whipped frosting is easiest for little fingers to sink into. Fondant looks polished, but it’s firm and slick, so babies often can’t get through it — and getting through it is half the fun.

For a session with us, the cake is already taken care of. If you’re also planning one for the party, a few simple choices help:

  • Light colors photograph beautifully. White, cream and soft pastels keep photos timeless, while deeply dyed frosting — bright red, royal blue, black — can tint cheeks, hands and clothes for a while.
  • Simple flavors are a common choice. Vanilla is a classic, and some families prefer a less-sweet recipe made with fruit such as banana or applesauce.
  • Leave off anything hard or inedible. Everything ends up in little hands and mouths, so skip toothpicks, dowels, wired sugar flowers, plastic toppers and hard candies.
  • Keep it cool on the drive home. Valley summers are hot, and soft frosting can slump quickly in a warm car.

If you have questions about allergies or about any ingredients, check with your pediatrician before the big day — they know your baby’s needs best. You’re always welcome to share any concerns with us when you book, too.

How a cake smash session works with Adrisabel

Here’s the part parents are usually happy to hear: you don’t need to order, pick up or carry in a cake. Every Cake Smash session includes one timeless cake, one timeless backdrop and eight edited photos of your birthday baby. We keep the setup clean and classic, so the pictures feel as lovely years from now as they do this week.

  1. Before: send a request through the Cake Smash booking form or call/text (409) 354-3075, and we’ll reply within 24 hours. Your date is held with a 50% deposit via Zelle, and the rest is due on session day.
  2. During: just bring your birthday baby — and maybe a change of clothes for the ride home. Adrisabel photographs every session herself and lets your little one explore at their own pace.
  3. After: before you head home, you’ll sit down with us and pick your favorites on the spot — no proof gallery waiting for you later. Each image is hand-selected, curated and edited, and the finished photos arrive within one week.

Can’t narrow it down to eight? You can add more edited photos to any session. Twin birthdays work, too: twins can join any package, with 4 extra photos included.

Dive in or careful poke — both make wonderful pictures

Every baby meets their smash cake differently. Some dive right in with both fists. Others take a careful first poke, study the frosting on one finger, and look to you before going back for more.

The bold ones give you a joyful mess; the cautious ones give you thoughtful, wide-eyed expressions that are every bit as sweet. A few small things help either way:

  • Let your baby set the pace. A slow start is normal, and coaxing too hard can make little ones pull back.
  • Stay where they can see you. A familiar face is reassuring in a new place.
  • Show them how. If they’re unsure, touching the frosting yourself is often all the invitation they need.
  • Let the mess happen. Frosting in the hair is part of the story — that’s what the change of clothes is for.

And if your baby decides the cake is far too strange to touch at all? Keep that photo, too. A puzzled stare over a perfect little cake can become the family favorite.

When to book your cake smash

Many families schedule the session a couple of weeks before the first birthday party. Since edited images arrive within one week, that leaves time to print a favorite for the party table or tuck one into thank-you notes.

We’re open Monday through Saturday by appointment and closed Sundays. The private studio is in the McAllen area (you’ll get the exact location once you book), and we welcome families from across the RGV. From Mission it’s about 10–20 minutes, and from Brownsville about 60–70 minutes, which is worth factoring in when you choose a time of day.

Want to see the setup first? Visit our cake smash photography page or browse real sessions in the portfolio. And if you’d love photos from the months before the birthday, too, our baby milestone sessions follow your little one through the first year.

When to take maternity photos: finding your sweet spot

A calm, practical guide to timing your maternity portraits — the weeks many families choose, when to go a little earlier, and how to line up your newborn session in the same step.

By Adrisabel · newborn & baby photographer · 15+ years of experience

As general guidance, many families take maternity photos between about 28 and 34 weeks of pregnancy. By then the bump is clearly visible, and moving around, standing and posing are usually still comfortable.

That window is a guide, not a deadline. If you’re deciding when to take maternity photos for your own pregnancy, this guide walks through why those weeks work so well and when going a little earlier makes sense. We’ll also cover what a studio session in the McAllen area is like, and how to save a spot for your newborn session at the same time — wherever in the Rio Grande Valley you call home.

In this guide

  1. Why 28–34 weeks is a common sweet spot
  2. When going a little earlier makes sense
  3. Why a studio session takes the pressure off
  4. Outfits, gowns and your timeline
  5. Bring your partner and the soon-to-be big siblings
  6. Reserve your newborn session at the same time
  7. Planning your drive to the studio
  8. Questions parents ask

Why 28–34 weeks is a common sweet spot

When to do maternity photos really depends on two things: your bump and your energy. Before about 28 weeks, many bumps are still small enough to disappear under a soft dress or a flowing gown. Over the following weeks the curve becomes clear from almost every angle — and that shape is what makes a maternity portrait feel like one.

At the other end, the last weeks of pregnancy often bring swelling, broken sleep and a body that would much rather rest. Portraits ask a little of you — standing, turning, shifting your weight — so it helps to schedule them while that still feels easy.

A simple way to think about the window:

  • Around 28–30 weeks: a defined bump and, for many people, steady energy.
  • Around 31–34 weeks: a fuller, rounder bump. Choose the time of day you usually feel your best.
  • Past 34 weeks: still possible for many families who feel well. Book it soon rather than waiting for the perfect week.

There’s a practical bonus, too. After every session, we sit together and help you choose your favorite images, and your edited photos are delivered within one week — so portraits taken in this window are ready well before your due date.

When going a little earlier makes sense

If you’re deciding when to get maternity photos with twins on the way, it’s common to plan a little earlier — often near the start of that window or just before it. Twin bumps tend to show sooner, and many parents find the final stretch more tiring.

The same thinking applies if your doctor suggests resting more, or if this pregnancy has simply felt heavier than you expected. Your doctor knows your situation best, so check with them if you’re unsure, then choose a date that suits your body rather than a chart.

A few signs it may be time to book sooner rather than later:

  • You’re carrying twins (or more).
  • Your doctor has mentioned taking it easy.
  • Being on your feet for a while already leaves you worn out.
  • You feel wonderful right now — which is a perfectly good reason, too.

Above all, listen to your body. The right week for your photos is the one when you feel comfortable enough to enjoy them.

Expecting?

Adrisabel photographs families from all over the Rio Grande Valley in her private studio in the McAllen area. Send a request or call/text (409) 354-3075.

Ask about maternity Maternity photography

Why a studio session takes the pressure off

Maternity sessions with Adrisabel take place in her private studio in the McAllen area, so there’s no Valley heat or wind to plan around. You won’t be checking the forecast all week, waiting for a cooler weekend or fixing your hair between gusts.

That matters for timing more than you might think. Weather-dependent plans have a way of slipping, and a delay of a few weeks can carry you past the window you hoped for. In the studio, the weather simply isn’t part of the decision.

It’s easier on your partner, too. Nobody enjoys standing outside in a long dress or a buttoned-up shirt in the afternoon heat. Indoors, you can both relax and enjoy the time together — you’ll find more about the session itself on our maternity photography page.

Outfits, gowns and your timeline

Studio gowns are available, and Adrisabel helps you plan outfits and colors that feel like you, so there’s no need to shop for anything special. If you do want to wear something of your own, though, the calendar matters more than you might expect.

Your bump keeps growing between the day you buy an outfit and the day of your session, so stretchy or adjustable pieces are a safer bet than something that fits perfectly today. Try everything on again about a week before.

For partners and kids, settle the colors early and do a quick try-on the week of the session. Little ones have a way of outgrowing things overnight.

Bring your partner and the soon-to-be big siblings

Partners and big brothers and sisters are welcome. A maternity session can be about the whole family getting ready to grow: a hand resting on the bump, a toddler curious about the baby inside, everyone close together.

If children are joining, a little planning helps them enjoy it:

  • Pick a time of day when they’re usually rested and happy.
  • Feed them before you leave and pack a tidy snack for the car.
  • Talk about the baby on the way — kids who feel part of the day tend to lean in naturally.
  • Let them warm up at their own pace. A shy start is completely normal.

In a few weeks, today’s big brother may be the one leaning in to kiss the baby. Photographing both chapters — the waiting and the welcome — tells the whole story.

Reserve your newborn session at the same time

Booking maternity is the perfect time to reserve your newborn session too. Newborn portraits are best in the first 5–14 days after birth, while babies are sleepy and curl up easily, and those days arrive quickly.

Here’s how it works. We save a spot around your due date, and when your baby arrives, you send us a message and we set the session within that 5–14 day window. Early or late babies are completely normal — the session is simply set when your little one is here.

There are two newborn sessions to choose from:

  • Sunshine (baby only): 8 edited photos, 2 outfits and 2 backdrops.
  • Wonderland (baby, siblings and parents): 15 edited photos, 2 outfits and 4 backdrops.

Both are on our newborn photography page, and our guide on when to do newborn photos has more on timing that first session. Expecting twins? They can be added to any package, with 4 extra photos included.

Planning your drive to the studio

Families come to the studio from all over the Rio Grande Valley. From McAllen and Pharr it’s just minutes; Mission is about 10–20 minutes away, Edinburg about 15–20 minutes, Harlingen about 40–45 minutes and Brownsville about 60–70 minutes.

If you’re coming from farther out, choose a time that leaves room for traffic and a stop to stretch your legs — long car rides can feel longer in the third trimester. Bring water, and plan to arrive a few minutes early so you can settle in without rushing.

When you’re ready, ask about a maternity session through our booking form, or call or text (409) 354-3075. We reply within 24 hours with maternity details and availability, and we can save your newborn spot in the same conversation. Frequently asked

How far is the studio from La Joya?

From La Joya, it’s a straight drive east on Expressway 83 (I-2/US 83) through Peñitas, Palmview and Mission, about 20–25 minutes, or closer to 30 at rush hour. The exact session location is shared after booking.

Can we schedule around rush hour on Expressway 83?

Yes. Sessions are booked Monday through Saturday by appointment, so you can ask for a time that misses the busiest traffic through Mission. Outside rush hour, the trip from La Joya is about 20–25 minutes; at peak times, allow closer to 30. A Saturday session is another easy option.

Can you photograph our newborn at home in La Joya?

Newborn sessions take place in our private studio in the McAllen area rather than at home. Wraps, outfits, bonnets, props, little beds and backdrops are already set up there, so all you bring from La Joya is your baby and a diaper bag. The only session held outside the studio is Seaside Beach, a family session on South Padre Island.

What if my baby arrives early or late?

That’s completely normal — babies keep their own schedule! Just let us know when your little one arrives and we’ll set your session within that ideal newborn window.

Is newborn photography safe?

Safety comes before any photo. With 15+ years of experience and hundreds of babies photographed, Adrisabel is trained in safe newborn posing: every pose is supported, the studio is kept warm and clean, and a parent is always close by.

When will I receive my photos?

Your edited images are delivered within one week of your session.

What is the Pixie Dust milestone package?

Pixie Dust is 5 milestone sessions during baby’s first year (babies 1–11 months). Choose one schedule — Option A: 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 months, or Option B: 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 months. Each session includes 8 edited images, 1 outfit and 1 backdrop, and siblings and parents are included. The 1-year Cake Smash is not included.

What is the best age for baby photos?

Every stage is worth celebrating! Our Fairytale session is made for babies 2–11 months — the months of first smiles, giggles and sitting up — and Cake Smash celebrates the first birthday.

For newborn and baby portraits, everything Adrisabel uses, from wraps and outfits to little beds and backdrops, is kept in our private studio in the McAllen area, so sessions stay there rather than at the Basilica, a park or your home. For a beach backdrop, there’s the Seaside Beach family session on South Padre Island.

What if my baby arrives early or late?

That’s completely normal — babies keep their own schedule! Just let us know when your little one arrives and we’ll set your session within that ideal newborn window.

Is newborn photography safe?

Safety comes before any photo. With 15+ years of experience and hundreds of babies photographed, Adrisabel is trained in safe newborn posing: every pose is supported, the studio is kept warm and clean, and a parent is always close by.

When will I receive my photos?

Your edited images are delivered within one week of your session.

What is the Pixie Dust milestone package?

Pixie Dust is 5 milestone sessions during baby’s first year (babies 1–11 months). Choose one schedule — Option A: 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 months, or Option B: 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 months. Each session includes 8 edited images, 1 outfit and 1 backdrop, and siblings and parents are included. The 1-year Cake Smash is not included.

What is the best age for baby photos?

Every stage is worth celebrating! Our Fairytale session is made for babies 2–11 months — the months of first smiles, giggles and sitting up — and Cake Smash celebrates the first birthday.

Privacy policy

Last updated: September 2026

This policy explains what information Adrisabel Photography (“we”, “us”) collects through adrisabel.com and how we use it. If you have any questions, contact us at adrianaisabelphoto@gmail.com or (409) 354-3075.

Information you give us

When you send a booking request or contact us, we collect the details you choose to share — such as your name, phone number, email address, the session you’re interested in, your preferred date and time, your baby’s due date or birthday, and any notes. Booking requests are delivered to our inbox through our form provider, Formspree.

How we use it

  • To reply to you, answer your questions and schedule your session.
  • To send you information about your booking and your photos.
  • To keep basic records of our sessions and payments.

We do not sell your personal information.

Analytics and advertising

Our website uses Google Tag Manager and related Google tools to understand how visitors use the site and to measure our advertising (for example, whether a booking request was sent after clicking an ad). These tools may use cookies or similar technologies. You can manage cookies in your browser settings and learn more about how Google uses information at policies.google.com.

Your choices

You may ask us to access, correct or delete the personal information you have shared with us by emailing adrianaisabelphoto@gmail.com.

Children’s privacy

Our website is intended for parents and guardians. We do not knowingly collect personal information directly from children.

Changes

We may update this policy from time to time. The date above shows when it was last changed.

What to expect

Barefoot, breezy & beautiful

Beach sessions are all about connection: walking hand in hand by the water, little feet in the sand, cuddles in the ocean breeze. We guide you gently the whole time, so even the littlest ones stay happy and relaxed.

We’ll plan the date and time with you for the softest light of the day, and share the exact meeting spot on the island when you book. After the session you’ll choose your favorite images, and your 15 edited photos arrive within one week.

  • Soft, coordinating colors look beautiful by the water

  • Grandparents and extended family are welcome

Do you offer beach sessions?

How do I reserve my session?

Send a request through our online booking form or call/text (409) 354-3075. We’ll confirm the date and time with you, and a 50% deposit via Zelle reserves your spot. The balance is due on session day.

Can I get more photos than my package includes?

Of course. Extra edited photos can be added to any session, so you never have to leave a favorite behind.

How do I choose my photos?

At the end of your session we sit together and help you pick your favorite images for editing. There’s no proof gallery to sort through at home — every image is hand-selected, curated and edited with care.

Common questions

Frequently asked

How much does newborn photography cost?

We offer two newborn packages: Sunshine (baby only · 8 edited photos · 2 outfits · 2 backdrops) and Wonderland with siblings and parents (15 edited photos · 2 outfits · 4 backdrops). Send a booking request or call/text (409) 354-3075 and we’ll share current package details. See all sessions.

How do I reserve my session?

Send a request through our online booking form or call/text (409) 354-3075. We’ll confirm the date and time with you, and a 50% deposit via Zelle reserves your spot. The balance is due on session day.

When should I book my newborn session?

Reach out during your second or third trimester so we can save a spot around your due date. Newborn portraits are best taken 5–14 days after birth, when babies are sleepiest and most comfortable in those soft, curled-up poses. Many families book maternity portraits at the same time.

How long does a newborn session take?

Newborn sessions usually take about 2–3 hours. We never rush — there’s time for feeding, cuddles, soothing and diaper changes, and your baby sets the pace.

Is newborn photography safe?

Safety comes before any photo. With 15+ years of experience and hundreds of babies photographed, Adrisabel is trained in safe newborn posing: every pose is supported, the studio is kept warm and clean, and a parent is always close by.

What is the Pixie Dust milestone package?

Pixie Dust is 5 milestone sessions during baby’s first year (babies 1–11 months). Choose one schedule — Option A: 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 months, or Option B: 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 months. Each session includes 8 edited images, 1 outfit and 1 backdrop, and siblings and parents are included. The 1-year Cake Smash is not included.

These moments won’t last forever

But your photos will. Reach out today to check availability and reserve your date — we’d love to capture this chapter with you.

How far is the studio from Brownsville?

Any month is a milestone! Fairytale sessions are for babies 2–11 months, Pixie Dust follows five milestones from 1 to 10 months, and Cake Smash celebrates the first birthday.

Do you provide outfits, wraps and props?

Yes. The studio is stocked with wraps, outfits, bonnets, headbands, little beds, baskets and backdrops in soft, timeless colors. You’re welcome to bring a meaningful item from home, too.

What is the best age for baby photos?

Every stage is worth celebrating! Our Fairytale session is made for babies 2–11 months — the months of first smiles, giggles and sitting up — and Cake Smash celebrates the first birthday.

What’s included in the Cake Smash session?

Cake Smash includes 1 timeless cake, 8 edited photos and 1 timeless backdrop. Just bring your birthday baby (and maybe a change of clothes for the ride home).

Common questions

Frequently asked questions

Everything you need to know before your newborn, baby, cake smash or beach session. Still wondering about something? Call or text (409) 354-3075.

Book your session Call or text

Booking & pricing

How much does newborn photography cost?

We offer two newborn packages: Sunshine (baby only · 8 edited photos · 2 outfits · 2 backdrops) and Wonderland with siblings and parents (15 edited photos · 2 outfits · 4 backdrops). Send a booking request or call/text (409) 354-3075 and we’ll share current package details. See all sessions.

How do I reserve my session?

Send a request through our online booking form or call/text (409) 354-3075. We’ll confirm the date and time with you, and a 50% deposit via Zelle reserves your spot. The balance is due on session day.

When should I book my newborn session?

Reach out during your second or third trimester so we can save a spot around your due date. Newborn portraits are best taken 5–14 days after birth, when babies are sleepiest and most comfortable in those soft, curled-up poses. Many families book maternity portraits at the same time.

What if my baby arrives early or late?

That’s completely normal — babies keep their own schedule! Just let us know when your little one arrives and we’ll set your session within that ideal newborn window.

Do you photograph twins?

Yes — double the love! Twin sessions can be added to any package and include 4 extra photos.

Can I get more photos than my package includes?

Of course. Extra edited photos can be added to any session, so you never have to leave a favorite behind.

Your session

How long does a newborn session take?

Newborn sessions usually take about 2–3 hours. We never rush — there’s time for feeding, cuddles, soothing and diaper changes, and your baby sets the pace.

Is newborn photography safe?

Safety comes before any photo. With 15+ years of experience and hundreds of babies photographed, Adrisabel is trained in safe newborn posing: every pose is supported, the studio is kept warm and clean, and a parent is always close by.

Do you provide outfits, wraps and props?

Yes. The studio is stocked with wraps, outfits, bonnets, headbands, little beds, baskets and backdrops in soft, timeless colors. You’re welcome to bring a meaningful item from home, too.

What should we bring to a newborn session?

Just your baby, feeding supplies, a pacifier if your baby uses one, and extra diapers. We take care of everything else.

What is the Pixie Dust milestone package?

Pixie Dust is 5 milestone sessions during baby’s first year (babies 1–11 months). Choose one schedule — Option A: 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 months, or Option B: 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 months. Each session includes 8 edited images, 1 outfit and 1 backdrop, and siblings and parents are included. The 1-year Cake Smash is not included.

What is the best age for baby photos?

Every stage is worth celebrating! Our Fairytale session is made for babies 2–11 months — the months of first smiles, giggles and sitting up — and Cake Smash celebrates the first birthday.

What’s included in the Cake Smash session?

Cake Smash includes 1 timeless cake, 8 edited photos and 1 timeless backdrop. Just bring your birthday baby (and maybe a change of clothes for the ride home).

Do you offer beach sessions?

Yes! Our Seaside Beach family session takes place at South Padre Island and includes 15 edited photos. See the beach session page for details.

Do you offer maternity photos?

Yes — maternity portraits are a beautiful way to begin your baby’s story, and many moms book their newborn session at the same time. Send us a message and we’ll share maternity details and availability.

Your photos

How do I choose my photos?

At the end of your session we sit together and help you pick your favorite images for editing. There’s no proof gallery to sort through at home — every image is hand-selected, curated and edited with care.

When will I receive my photos?

Your edited images are delivered within one week of your session.

Location

Where are sessions held?

We serve families across the whole Rio Grande Valley — especially McAllen, Mission, Pharr, Edinburg and Brownsville. The exact session location is shared after booking.

What areas do you serve?

The whole Rio Grande Valley — McAllen, Mission, Pharr, Edinburg, Brownsville, Harlingen, Weslaco, San Juan, Alamo, Donna, Mercedes, Sharyland, Rio Grande City and beyond — and our Seaside Beach sessions take place on South Padre Island. See all the areas we serve.

Newborn days, first smiles, the big first birthday — reach out today and let’s plan the perfect session for your little one.
